AI Clinical Decision Support Lite  
1. Executive Overview  
The AI Clinical Decision Support Lite Hackathon is a specialized 5 -day technical 
competition.  
The goal is to design and implement a Retrieval -Augmented Generation (RAG) system 
that delivers evidence -based clinical recommendations  
grounded strictly in off icial medical guidelines.  
2. The Challenge  
Large Language Models (LLMs) can generate fluent medical advice, but they often 
"hallucinate" or provide unsupported claims.  
Participants must build a system that:  
• Ingests official medical PDFs.  
• Retrieves only  relevant, high -quality evidence.  
• Generates responses strictly based on that evidence.  
• Provides transparent citations (Document Name, Section, Page).  
3. Content & Technical Requirements  
Teams must develop a 4 -layer architecture:  
1. Document Ingestion L ayer:  PDF parsing, section -aware chunking, and vector 
indexing.

3. Content & Technical Requirements  
Teams must develop a 4 -layer architecture:  
1. Document Ingestion L ayer:  PDF parsing, section -aware chunking, and vector 
indexing.  
2. Retrieval Layer:  Semantic search optimization and transparent chunk display.  
3. Generation Layer : Strict grounding prompts and structured citation formatting.  
4. Safety Layer:  Hallucination  detection and refusal mechanisms for out -of-scope 
queries.  
 
 
 
 
 
4. 5-Day Timeline  
Day 1 — Research,  Scope  & Document  Ingestion  
Objective:  Define  clinical  scope  and build  a reliable  ingestion  pipeline.  
Tasks : 
• Select  1–2 official  guideline  PDFs.  
• Verify  public  accessibility  and legal  usability.  
• Parse  PDF content  (structured  extraction  preferred).  
• Implement  section -aware  chunking.  
• Generate  embeddings.  
• Index  chunks  in vector  database.  
• Store  metadata  (document  name,  section,  page  number).

• Implement  section -aware  chunking.  
• Generate  embeddings.  
• Index  chunks  in vector  database.  
• Store  metadata  (document  name,  section,  page  number).  
End-of-Day Outcome:  Fully  indexed  guideline  corpus  and retriev al-ready  vector  
database.  
Day 2 — Retrieval  Optimization  
Objective:  Achieve  high -precision  evidence  retrieval.  
Tasks:  
• Implement  top-k semantic  search.  
• Tune  chunk  size and overlap.  
• Adjust  k-value.  
• Evaluate  embedding  model  choice.  
• Log retrieval  scores.  
• Display  retrieved  chunks  before  generation.  
End-of-Day Outcome:  Stable  and explainable  retrieval  layer  with  evaluation  logs.  
Day 3 — Grounded  Generation  & Citation  
Objective:  Generate  structured  answers  strictly  grounded  in retrieved  evidence.  
Tasks:  
• Design  strict  grounding  prompts.  
• Prohibit  external  knowledge  use. 
• Format  citations  clearly  (document  name,  section,  page  number).

Tasks:  
• Design  strict  grounding  prompts.  
• Prohibit  external  knowledge  use. 
• Format  citations  clearly  (document  name,  section,  page  number).  
• Structure  response  (recommendation,  excerpt,  citation).  
• Implement  refusal  behavior  when  context  is insufficient.  
End-of-Day Outcome: Fully  functional  RAG  pipeline  with  proper  citation  and refusal 
mechanism.  
Day 4 — Safety,  Guardrails  & Internal  Evaluation  
Objective:  Improve  reliability  and quantify  performance.  
Tasks:  
• Add retrieval  confidence  threshold.  
• Implement  unsupported  claim  detection.  
• Test  with  in-scope,  ambiguous,  and out-of-domain  queries.  
• Measure  Retrieval  Precision  @ k. 
• Measure  citation  accuracy.  
• Evaluate  faithfulness  to retrieved  text.  
End-of-Day Outcome: Evaluated  and stress -tested  system  with  prepared  safety 
demonstrations.  
Day 5 — Final  Presentation  & Judge  Evaluation

• Evaluate  faithfulness  to retrieved  text.  
End-of-Day Outcome: Evaluated  and stress -tested  system  with  prepared  safety 
demonstrations.  
Day 5 — Final  Presentation  & Judge  Evaluation  
Objective:  Demonstrate  transparency,  safety,  and system  rigor.  
Presentation  Requirements  (15–30 minutes  per team):  
• Problem  & Scope  (clinical  topic  and guideline  source).  
• System  Architecture  (ingestion,  retrieval,  generation,  safety).  
• Live Demonstration  with  judge -provided  query.  
• Display  retrieved  chunks.  
• Generated  structured  response  with  citation.  
• Refusal  case  demonstration.  
5. Selection Stages  
1. Initial Screening:  Verification of technical skills (Python/APIs) and team 
composition (2 –4 members).  
2. Scope Approval (Day 1):  Mentors review and approve the chosen clinical 
guidelines for legal and technical suitability.  
3. Technical Milestone (Day 3):  Internal review of the functional RAG pipeline and

guidelines for legal and technical suitability.  
3. Technical Milestone (Day 3):  Internal review of the functional RAG pipeline and 
citation accuracy.  
4. Final Evaluation (Day 5):  Live presentation and stress -testing by the judging 
panel.  
6. Judging Criteria (100 Points)  
• Retrieval Precision (30 pts): Accuracy of the evidence surfaced.  
• Answer Grounding & Citations (25 pts):  No hallucinations and precise source 
tracking.  
• Architecture Design (15 pts):  Technical clarity and modularity.  
• Evaluation Metrics (15 pts):  Quality of the team’s internal testing methodology.  
• Clinical Safety (10 pts): Proper handling of insufficient evidence.  
• UX & Live Demo (5 pts):  System us ability and performance under pressure.  
7. Staff Roles  
• Mentor:  Provides technical guidance on RAG logic and ensures teams stay within 
the medical scope.  
• Trainer:  Conducts workshops on prompt engineering, embeddings, and medical 
AI safety.

• Mentor:  Provides technical guidance on RAG logic and ensures teams stay within 
the medical scope.  
• Trainer:  Conducts workshops on prompt engineering, embeddings, and medical 
AI safety.  
• Operations:  Manag es the event schedule, logistics, and communication between 
teams and judges.  
8. Recommended Data Sources  
U.S. Preventive  Services  Task  Force  (USPSTF)  Recommendations  
What  it is: The gold  standard  for preventive  medicine  in the United  States,  covering 
screenings, counseling, and preventive medications.  
Why it’s perfect for RAG: The documents are strictly structured, publicly funded (no 
copyright  hurdles  for educational  use),  and feature  explicit  letter  grades  (A, B, C, D, I) for 
the strength of the evidence.  
Where  to find it: USPSTF  Recommendation  Topics  
 
 
 
NICE  Guidance  Portals  (UK)  
What  it is: The UK’s  National  Institute  for Health  and Care Excellence  provides

Where  to find it: USPSTF  Recommendation  Topics  
 
 
 
NICE  Guidance  Portals  (UK)  
What  it is: The UK’s  National  Institute  for Health  and Care Excellence  provides  
comprehensive,  evidence -based  guidance  for health  and social  care.  
Why  it’s perfect  for RAG:  NICE  documents  are legendary  for their  rigorous  formatting.  
They separate 'Recommendations' from 'Context' and 'Evidence,' making chunking and 
embedding highly predictable.  
Where  to find it: NICE  Published  Guidance  
WHO  Institutional  Repository  for Inform ation  Sharing  (IRIS)  
What  it is: The official  digital  library  of the World  Health  Organization's  published  
material and clinical guidelines.  
Why  it’s perfect  for RAG:  It offers  a massive  array  of global  health  topics.  The PDFs  
are open -access,  clearly  cited,  and often  come  with  executive  summaries  that are 
great  for testing retrieval accuracy.  
Where  to find it: WHO  IRIS Portal

Where  to find it: WHO  IRIS Portal  
European  Society  of Cardiology  (ESC)  Clinical  Practice  Guidelines  
What  it is: The leading  authority  on cardiovascular  care  in Europe.  
Why  it’s perfect  for RAG:  Their  guidelines  are incredibly  visual  and structured,  and they  
use a strict color -coded class of recommendation and level of evidence system. This is a 
great stress test to see if a RAG system can accurately extract the specific class of 
evidence.  
Where  to find it: ESC Guidelines  
MAGICapp  (Making  GRADE  the Irresistible  Choice)

publish here.
